fields.subject: SQL Server Type Mapping
fields.trigger: a caller invokes a scalar input or output helper for a query contract
fields.response: append one SQL Server parameter to the supplied collection using the helper's selected SQL type and direction, then return that collection
fields.postcondition: the parameter name is @-prefixed; input helpers preserve supplied values except that a null reference value is represented as database null, and specifically for the non-nullable double, float and Guid input overloads, double.NaN, float.NaN and Guid.Empty are likewise represented as database null; the corresponding nullable double?, float? and Guid? input overloads instead preserve the value as-is whenever HasValue is true — including a NaN or Guid.Empty value — and represent only a HasValue-false nullable as database null. This split is deliberate (by design, not a defect): a non-nullable value has no other way to express database null, so its sentinel mirrors the read side (GetDouble/GetFloat return NaN and GetGuid returns Guid.Empty for a database null), whereas a caller holding a nullable type has a real null and so can send NaN or Guid.Empty as a value; the XML documentation of the non-nullable overloads states this in a remarks section. Output helpers omit an input value and retain requested size, ANSI locale, or decimal precision and scale where their type requires it
